title: Serre duality
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth proper curve over $k$, of pure dimension
$n\in\{0,1\}$, and $\cF$ a finite locally free $\cO_X$-module. With
$\omega_X=\Omega^n_{X/k}$ the canonical module, let
$t_X:H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$ be the *trace*: for $n=0$,
$X=\Spec A$ with $A$ finite étale over $k$, $\omega_X=\cO_X$ and
$t_X=\operatorname{Tr}_{A/k}$; for $n=1$ and $X$ integral with function
field $K$, the residue sequence
$0\to\omega_X\to\underline{\Omega^1_{K/k}}\to\bigoplus_{x}i_{x,*}\bigl(\Omega^1_{K/k}/\omega_{X,x}\bigr)\to0$
($x$ over the closed points; the constant sheaf in the middle is flasque) identifies
$H^1(X,\omega_X)$ with the cokernel of
$\Omega^1_{K/k}\to\bigoplus_x\Omega^1_{K/k}/\omega_{X,x}$, and
$t_X\bigl((\eta_x)_x\bigr)=\sum_x\operatorname{res}_x(\eta_x)$, where
$\operatorname{res}_x:\Omega^1_{K/k}\to k$ is Tate's $k$-linear residue
at $x$: it kills $\omega_{X,x}$, it satisfies the residue theorem
$\sum_x\operatorname{res}_x(\eta)=0$ for $\eta\in\Omega^1_{K/k}$, and it
equals $\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(x)/k}$ of the classical residue
(computed in $\widehat{\cO}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[t]]$) whenever
$\kappa(x)/k$ is separable, hence at every $x$ when $k$ is perfect. The residue theorem is exactly what makes
$t_X$ well defined on the cokernel. (The naive formula
$\sum_x\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(x)/k}\circ\operatorname{res}_x$ is not
available over imperfect $k$: at a closed point with $\kappa(x)/k$
inseparable, $\widehat{\cO}_{X,x}$ has no coefficient field containing
$k$, and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(x)/k}$ vanishes on a purely
inseparable extension; Tate's residue avoids both problems.) For a possibly disconnected $X$ of pure dimension one, use this construction on each connected component $X_j$ (each is integral), identify $H^1(X,\omega_X)=\bigoplus_j H^1(X_j,\omega_{X_j})$, and set $t_X=\sum_jt_{X_j}$. For $X=\varnothing$ the trace is zero. Cohomology in negative degrees is understood to be zero. Then the
trace pairing

$$
H^q(X,\cF)\otimes_kH^{n-q}(X,\cF^{\vee}\otimes\omega_X)
\xrightarrow{\ \cup\ }H^n(X,\cF\otimes\cF^{\vee}\otimes\omega_X)
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{ev}\ }H^n(X,\omega_X)\xrightarrow{\ t_X\ }k
$$

is perfect for every $q$:

$$
H^q(X,\cF)^{\vee}\ \cong\ H^{n-q}\bigl(X,\cF^{\vee}\otimes\omega_X\bigr),
$$

and this isomorphism is natural in $\cF$: for a morphism
$\varphi:\cF\to\mathcal G$ of finite locally free modules,
$\langle\varphi_*a,b\rangle=\langle a,(\varphi^{\vee}\otimes1)_*b\rangle$,
i.e. it carries $H^q(\varphi)^{\vee}$ to
$H^{n-q}(\varphi^{\vee}\otimes1)$. In particular ($n=1$, $q=1$,
$\cF=\cO_X$), $H^1(X,\cO_X)^{\vee}\cong H^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k})$: for a
smooth proper connected curve over algebraically closed $k$ the genus
$\dim_kH^0(C,\Omega^1_{C/k})$ of [sk-def-curve] equals
$\dim_kH^1(C,\cO_C)$, the genus of the conventions of this section.

proof.text: The structure morphism is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] its local rings are regular local rings, hence domains by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. The connected components are finite in number and open by [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open]; they are closed since the complement is the union of the other components. Distinct irreducible components cannot meet, since such a local ring would have two minimal primes; thus each nonempty connected component is integral. The categories of module sheaves and their global-sections functors on a finite clopen union are componentwise products: restriction and extension by zero are inverse equivalences, and sections are tuples. Module sheaves have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. A tuple of injectives is injective because any lifting problem extends in each coordinate. Injective resolutions can consequently be taken componentwise, giving $H^q(X,E)=\bigoplus_jH^q(X_j,E|_{X_j})$. Cup products, evaluation and duals are also componentwise. A finite orthogonal sum of perfect pairings is perfect, with inverse the tuple of the inverses. We may therefore work on a nonempty integral component and sum at the end; the empty case has only zero vector spaces.

source.place: Component reduction; fills in the integral parenthesis of the statement without adding a connectedness hypothesis.

proof.text: For $n=1$, the integral component is a curve over $k$, and [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one] with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes its structure morphism smooth of relative dimension one. Thus [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] makes $\omega=\Omega^1_{X/k}$ locally free of rank one. Set $D(E)=E^\vee\otimes\omega$. Local dual bases show that $D(E)$ is finite locally free and that the evaluation map $D(D(E))\to E$ is an isomorphism: in a frame it is the usual double-dual identification followed by cancellation of the one-dimensional factor $\omega^\vee\otimes\omega$. These identifications commute with change of frames and morphisms. For $n=0$ use $\omega=\mathcal O_X$ and ordinary double duals. Finite locally free modules are quasi-coherent of finite type in these frames and hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Their cohomology is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-coherent-hi], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The dimension bound [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^q(X,E)=0$ for $q>n$; negative cohomology is zero by convention. These observations apply to $E$, $D(E)$ and $\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Canonical module, finite-dimensionality and degrees outside [0,n].

proof.text: Suppose $n=0$. By [lem-pc-dim-zero-finite-over-field], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite-dimensional over $k$. Smoothness of relative dimension zero is étaleness by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $P=\Gamma(X,E)$, [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective] gives a finitely presented projective $A$-module. The affine equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies $H^0(X,E^\vee)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$, and evaluation with $(\lambda,m)\mapsto\lambda(m)$. The trace form on $A$ is nondegenerate by [lem-sbc-trace-form-nondegenerate-iff-etale-field]. Hence the form on $A^N$ paired with its $A$-dual by $\operatorname{Tr}_{A/k}\sum_i\lambda_i m_i$ is perfect. Choose a surjection $A^N\to P$ from finite generators and split it by projectivity, giving a finite projective complement $P'$ with $P\oplus P'\cong A^N$. Its dual decomposes as $P^\vee\oplus(P')^\vee$, with cross terms zero; the inverse of the perfect map on $A^N$ respects these two summands, so its restriction proves perfection for $P$. By [lem-sc-scalar-cup-zero-global-sections], the degree-zero cup is the tensor of global sections, so this is exactly the requested trace pairing. Higher cohomology vanishes by step 2. For any $A$-linear $f:P\to Q$, $\lambda(f(m))=(\lambda\circ f)(m)$ proves its naturality, including after applying the trace.

source.place: Dimension zero: finite étale algebra trace.

proof.text: Now let $n=1$. For every closed point $x$, the local ring $O_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a regular local ring of dimension one (the chain from the generic point to $x$ has length one, and no chain can be longer since $\dim X=1$), hence a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]; on an affine neighbourhood the closed point is a maximal ideal of a finitely generated $k$-algebra, so its residue field is finite over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]. Apply [lem-pc-vector-bundle-principal-parts] first to $\mathcal O_X$: rational functions lie in almost every $O_x$, the intersection is $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and the principal-parts cokernel is $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Both are finite-dimensional by step 2. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-pc-tate-adelic-reciprocity] holds and the sum of local Tate residues of a rational differential is zero. Apply the same principal-parts resolution to $\omega$. By [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus] each residue kills $\omega_x$, so the sum defines a linear map from $\bigoplus_x\Omega^1_{K/k}/\omega_x$ to $k$; reciprocity says that it kills the image of $\Omega^1_{K/k}$. It therefore descends uniquely to $t_X:H^1(X,\omega)\to k$, with exactly the formula in the statement. The last clause of the local-calculus node gives the classical coefficient/field-trace formula precisely when $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable, with no perfection assumption on $k$.

source.place: Residue sequence and residue theorem; Tate §3, Theorem 3 and corollary.

proof.text:
The trace just constructed is nonzero. Indeed [lem-pc-dense-separable-points] supplies a closed point $x$ with finite separable $\kappa(x)/k$, since $X$ is smooth and nonempty. The trace form of this finite étale field algebra is nondegenerate by [lem-sbc-trace-form-nondegenerate-iff-etale-field], so there exists $ ar u\in\kappa(x)$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(x)/k}( ar u)
e0$ (pair with $1
e0$). Lift $ ar u$ to $u\in O_x$ and take a uniformizer $t$. The principal part $ut^{-1}dt$ at $x$, and zero elsewhere, represents a class of $H^1(X,\omega)$ by [lem-pc-vector-bundle-principal-parts]. By [lem-pc-tate-dvr-residue-calculus] its trace is $\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(x)/k}( ar u)
e0$. This argument uses a separable closed point only for this witness; it does not discard any inseparable points from the residue sum.

source.place: Nonzero residue trace: local uniformizer formula; cf. live Curve/ResidueTrace.lean, residueTrace_ne_zero.

proof.text:
We need only the dimension equality supplied by the existing projective-line route, not an identification of its abstract trace. Extend $k$ to an algebraic closure $\bar k$. The scheme $Y=X_{\bar k}$ is proper and smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]; the differential comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] identifies $\omega_Y$ with the pullback of $\omega_X$, and a local frame identifies pullback duals and tensor products with the dual and tensor product of the pullbacks. By [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one], $Y$ is smooth of relative dimension one. This condition restricts to each open connected component; [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field] makes every nonempty such component one-dimensional. Thus each is a proper smooth connected curve, as required below. Apply [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] over the algebraically closed field $\bar k$ to each component and add the dimensions using the product calculation of step 1. This yields $\dim_{\bar k}H^1(Y,E_{\bar k})=\dim_{\bar k}H^0(Y,D(E)_{\bar k})$. By [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent], both groups are obtained from the corresponding groups on $X$ by tensoring with $\bar k$. A $k$-basis stays a $\bar k$-basis after scalar extension, so
$$\dim_kH^1(X,E)=\dim_kH^0(X,D(E)).$$
All uses of [thm-sc-serre-duality-curve] occur over $\bar k$, respecting its current statement rather than silently substituting its newer arbitrary-field blueprint update. That theorem follows the stipulated projective-line duality/cohomology route.

source.place: Projective-line duality route via the existing curve theorem; flat extension used only for dimensions.

proof.text: For a nonzero sheaf map $b:E\to\omega$, its generic-stalk map is nonzero: in local frames, a map to a line bundle is a row of elements of a domain, and a row vanishing in the fraction field is zero. Write $B=\operatorname{im}b$, $N=\ker b$ and $Q=\operatorname{coker}b$. They are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum], since $B=\ker(\omega\to Q)$. At the generic point the nonzero map to the one-dimensional space $\omega_\eta$ is surjective, so $Q$ is supported on a closed subset of dimension zero: locally the nonvanishing of a row entry makes $Q=0$, and locally the support of $Q$ is the zero set of all row entries, hence is closed. A proper closed subset of an integral one-dimensional space has dimension zero: a strict specialization chain inside it could be prefixed by the generic point and would contradict $\dim X=1$. By [lem-sc-support-dimension-cohomology-vanishing] and [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology], $H^1(X,Q)=0$. Also $H^2(X,N)=0$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension]. Module sheaves have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives] and global sections is additive left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. The two long exact sequences of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] for $0\to N\to E\to B\to0$ and $0\to B\to\omega\to Q\to0$ give surjections $H^1(E)\to H^1(B)\to H^1(\omega)$. Thus $H^1(b)$ is surjective.

source.place: Elementary use of two exact sequences and the cited dimension bounds; agent completion of the trace-pairing argument.

proof.text: Identify $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,\omega)=H^0(X,E^\vee\otimes\omega)$ by [lem-sc-ext-locally-free] in degree zero. The map $b\mapsto t_X\circ H^1(b)$ into $H^1(X,E)^\vee$ is injective: a nonzero $b$ has surjective $H^1(b)$ by step 7, whereas $t_X\ne0$ by step 5. It is an isomorphism by the finite-dimensional equality of step 6. By both formulas of [lem-sc-scalar-ext-cup-degree-zero], cup with a degree-zero class is the cohomology map of tensoring with that section, on either side; [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations] then applies the quotient to tensor over $\mathcal O_X$. In particular, cup with the global Hom class $b$ followed by evaluation is composition with $b$; evaluation after $s\mapsto s\otimes b$ is $s\mapsto b(s)$. Consequently its evaluated cup on $a\in H^1(E)$ is $H^1(b)(a)$, so this is precisely the asserted $q=1$ trace pairing. Finite-dimensional duality also makes its transpose perfect. Apply this result to $D(E)$: under $D(D(E))\cong E$, the transpose is the $q=0$ pairing for $E$. In local dual frames both evaluations send $s\otimes\lambda\otimes w$ to $\lambda(s)w$; the two degree-zero formulas just cited identify the swapped pairings without a sign. This proves the requested pairing for both remaining degrees.

source.place: Elementary assembly of injectivity, dimension equality, cup/evaluation and biduality.

proof.text:
For $\varphi:E\to G$ and a class $b$ with values in $G^\vee\otimes\omega$, [lem-sc-scalar-cup-coefficient-naturality] and the identity $\mathrm{ev}_G\circ(\varphi\otimes1)=\mathrm{ev}_E\circ(1\otimes(\varphi^\vee\otimes1))$ give
$$t_X\mathrm{ev}_G(\varphi_*a\smile b)=t_X\mathrm{ev}_E(a\smile(\varphi^\vee\otimes1)_*b).$$
The evaluation identity is checked on a local section $s$ and a functional $\lambda$: both sides equal $\lambda(\varphi(s))$. This is the naturality square for the isomorphism induced by the perfect pairing. The component sum in step 1 preserves this equality. Taking $E=\mathcal O_X$, $n=q=1$, and identifying $\mathcal O_X^\vee\otimes\omega_X=\omega_X$ gives $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)^\vee\cong H^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k})$. Equality of the two genus dimensions follows by taking dimensions and using [sk-def-curve].
